lane: tectonic-geomorphology: channel steepness (ksn) and knickpoints, not scarp shape
hypothesis: Bedrock channels that cross an active normal fault carry an upstream-steepening knickpoint; a knickpoint corroborated by >=3 independent drainage networks inside a strike-aligned corridor marks a fault trace, including traces absent from the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue.
mechanism: Fault-crossing channels record a step in rock-uplift rate as a step in normalized steepness ksn = S*(A/A0)^theta along chi (Kirby & Whipple 2012; Perron & Royden 2013). Single-channel knickpoints are ambiguous; strike-aligned corroboration across drainage divides is not, because no single-channel process is strike-aligned.
named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contact / basin-fill boundary: a hard-to-soft rock contact also steps ksn and can be strike-aligned across drainages. Secondary mimics: closed-basin (playa) base level, ephemeral/alluvial reaches, regional climate-precipitation gradient, and post-wildfire or landslide-derived steepening.
confound_controls: climate/regional gradient: knickpoint magnitude is z-scored inside 40 km blocks (blockwise_zscore), never ranked globally
playa / closed-basin base level: cells whose priority-flood raise exceeds 20 m are excluded (542,309 px measured)
lithology / basin fill: cells with depth_to_base_surf above its 90th footprint percentile are excluded (thick sedimentary cover = no bedrock channel)
ephemeral / alluvial: cells with cond_surf above its 95th percentile are excluded (clay-rich, evaporitic, non-bedrock)
channel-hood: only pixels with contributing area >= 20 cells (0.20 km^2) are eligible

declared_parameters.band: 12 det_elev (Detrended elevation - topography with regional trends removed)

first_test_mandated_by_brief.question: Do channels crossing withheld fault segments show larger steepness steps than random lines of the same orientation?
first_test_mandated_by_brief.statistic: mean log(ksn_up/ksn_down) over channel pixels within 3 px of the segment, paired against 15 random transects of identical length and orientation inside the fold's scored domain, >=10 px from any visible fault and from any withheld pixel
first_test_mandated_by_brief.pairing: per withheld connected component (>=6 px), pooled over all 16 fold cells (2 seeds x 4 quadrants x 2 modes)
first_test_mandated_by_brief.decision_rule: PROCEED only if the pooled mean paired difference > 0 AND its 95% percentile bootstrap CI over components excludes 0. Otherwise STOP and report the negative result as the deliverable.
first_test_mandated_by_brief.orientation_source: primary: principal axis of the withheld component (diagnostic, uses truth orientation); secondary/production-legal: strike of the nearest visible catalogue pixel via the structure tensor

leakage_canary: each feature alone is scored by AUC against withheld truth inside the fold domain; max(AUC, 1-AUC) > 0.90 is treated as leakage until proven otherwise

holdout.evaluator: src/gems57/evaluate_holdout.py (gems57-pooled-hide-v2), reused unmodified from the sibling template
holdout.design: hide whole catalogue segments with a 12 px domain erosion; all catalogue features from visible faults only; visible faults masked pixel-exactly; pooled DTI alpha=0.2 beta=0.8 300 m triangular kernel
holdout.budget_rule: fixed density = production_dot_budget / allowed footprint cells, applied per cell; k_truth for the marginal bar is estimated leave-one-out from the other cells' design prevalence, never from the scored cell's own truth count

uniqueness_gate.corpus: evidence/registry_full_index.json (655 pinned grid rasters across 56 sibling repositories), fetched and sha256-verified by scripts/fetch_registry_rasters.py
uniqueness_gate.checked: on the surface before placement and on the final dots
